A package propagates to a target when biocUniTools::get_candidates(), which has all the propagation criteria, selects it for that target. Yes links to the file that would be harvested. No links to the package’s R Universe job for that target.

Commit: the commits R Universe and BBS built. They must be the same for a package to propagate.
Source needs a passing R Universe source build (R CMD build, which builds vignettes), a passing R CMD check on Linux x86_64, and the same commit as BBS.
Windows x86_64 and macOS binaries need a passing source build, a binary that passed R CMD check and built, the same commit as BBS, and a platform the package supports.
Bioconductor only distributes binaries of software packages, so binaries of other package types show —.
Deprecated packages can propagate; they are marked so they can be skipped.

Legend


BBS: the first stage that fails: install, build, or check, with ERROR or TIMEOUT. Links to the BBS log.
R Universe: the first job that fails: source build or check, with ERROR, FAIL, or TIMEOUT, or the overall status if only that failed. Links to the job.
R Universe error: the step that failed and the likely cause, found in the job’s log. Links to the log. Expand a row to see the first error lines. Causes:

Hub resource: an ExperimentHub or AnnotationHub download failed.
Network/web service: a download or web service failed.
Missing package: a package is not available, for example archived on CRAN.
Missing cached data: data the package expects in a cache was missing.
External tool: Python, Java, Conda, LaTeX, or a command line tool.
Dependency changed: a function or class the package uses changed or was removed.
Timeout: the job ran out of time.
Test expectation failed: a test’s result no longer matched.
Other: none of the above, often a bug in the package.

Downloads / month: distinct IPs downloading the package from Bioconductor in the last 12 months, divided by 12.
Strong reverse deps: Bioconductor packages that depend on, import, or link to the package. Expand a row to see them and the packages that suggest it.
Mentions (R Universe _mentions): mentions in scientific papers.
Commits (12 weeks) (R Universe _updates): commits in the last 12 weeks, a sign the maintainer is working on the package.

title: Getting started with biocUniTools
text:
biocUniTools is a package for working with Bioconductor build data in R Universe. In this vignette, we’ll get build results from the Bioconductor Build System (BBS) and R Universe for comparison.
library(biocUniTools)

title: Getting started with biocUniTools
text:
Bioconductor branches and package types
uni_for_bioc() gives the Bioconductor version, R version, and universe for a branch.

bu <- uni_for_bioc("devel")
bu

$bioc_version
[1] "3.24"

$bioc_branch
[1] "devel"

$universe
[1] "bioc"

$r_version
[1] "4.6.0"


bioc_manifest() lists the packages of a type in a branch.

experiments <- bioc_manifest("devel", "data-experiment")
head(experiments)

[1] "affydata"                "AffymetrixDataTestFiles"
[3] "ALL"                     "ALLMLL"                 
[5] "AmpAffyExample"          "beta7"

title: Getting started with biocUniTools
text:
BBS results
bbs_nodes() lists the BBS build machines for a type.

bbs_nodes("devel", "data-experiment")

       node                         os   arch         platform
1 nebbiolo2 Linux (Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS) x86_64 x86_64-linux-gnu
                          r_version
1 4.6.1 (2026-06-24) -- "Happy Hop"


bbs_status() returns one row per package from one build machine. By default, it shows the builder for Linux x86_64. It has the version and commit the BBS built plus the result of each stage.

bbs <- bbs_status("devel", "data-experiment")
head(bbs[, c("Package", "Version", "commit", "install", "build", "check")])

           Package Version  commit install build check
1              ALL  1.55.0 c705298      OK    OK    OK
2           ALLMLL  1.53.0 c02b4ee      OK    OK    OK
3         ARRmData  1.49.0 359b678      OK    OK    OK
4        ASICSdata  1.33.0 a4b6bb4      OK    OK    OK
5 AWAggregatorData   1.3.0 1ef37b1      OK    OK    OK
6 Affyhgu133A2Expr  1.49.0 f0c221f      OK    OK    OK

title: Getting started with biocUniTools
text:
R Universe results
uni_jobs() downloads R Universe data for a branch. It can download jobs for all packages in a universe or a vector of packages.

jobs <- uni_jobs("devel", packages = experiments)

uni_status() returns one row per package type.
Note: source_build is the result of R CMD build on the source package to build vignettes in R Universe. check is the result of R CMD check of the Linux x86_64 binary job.

uni <- uni_status("devel", "data-experiment", jobs = jobs)
head(uni[, c("Package", "Version", "commit", "status", "source_build", "check",
             "bioccheck")])

           Package Version  commit  status source_build   check bioccheck
1              ALL  1.55.0 c705298 success           OK    NOTE     ERROR
2           ALLMLL  1.53.0 c02b4ee success           OK    NOTE     ERROR
3         ARRmData  1.49.0 359b678 success           OK    NOTE     ERROR
4        ASICSdata  1.33.0 a4b6bb4 success           OK WARNING   WARNING
5 AWAggregatorData   1.3.0 1ef37b1 success           OK      OK      NOTE
6 Affyhgu133A2Expr  1.49.0 f0c221f success           OK      OK     ERROR

title: Getting started with biocUniTools
section: Comparing results between the BBS and R Universe
text:
Comparing results between the BBS and R Universe
compare_builds() joins both results by package. It adds whether both systems built the same commit and whether they have the same result. Results are compared after normalize_result(), which treats NOTE as OK and WARNING(S) the same.

normalize_result(c("OK", "NOTE", "WARNINGS", "WARNING", "ERROR"))

[1] "OK"      "OK"      "WARNING" "WARNING" "ERROR"  



cmp <- compare_builds("devel", "data-experiment", bbs = bbs, uni = uni)
head(cmp[, c("Package", "where", "commit_match", "bbs_result", "uni_result",
             "result_match")])

           Package where commit_match bbs_result uni_result result_match
1              ALL  both         TRUE         OK       NOTE         TRUE
2           ALLMLL  both         TRUE         OK       NOTE         TRUE
3         ARRmData  both         TRUE         OK       NOTE         TRUE
4        ASICSdata  both         TRUE         OK    WARNING        FALSE
5 AWAggregatorData  both         TRUE         OK         OK         TRUE
6 Affyhgu133A2Expr  both         TRUE         OK         OK         TRUE


For workflows, the BBS does not run R CMD check, so compare_builds() compares R CMD build.
compare_summary() counts the matches and differences.

compare_summary(cmp)

  branch            type packages both bbs_only universe_only commits_match
1  devel data-experiment      442  422       19             1           421
  commits_differ results_match results_differ check_diverged
1              1           331             87              1

title: Getting started with biocUniTools
text:
Reports
The BBS and R Universe report pages on the biocUniTools website are made from this data. Their source is on the reports branch of the biocUniTools repository. write_comparisons() saves a comparison for every branch and type listed in a YAML configuration, and the report pages read the saved files:

write_comparisons("reports/config.yml")

compare_table(), compare_header(), compare_bars(), and compare_details() make the parts of each page, so you can use them in your own reports.
